title: Qualification rules for except/unless/provided-that, closed as two opposite-polarity condition classes, not one
goal: Close the repo's oldest open todo for 'except'/'unless'/'provided that' qualification clauses -- correctly, which the stub's own wording (treat all three the same) would not have done. Generalize lab.common.inference's exception mechanism to recognize CONDITION_POSITIVE (provided that/only if/as long as/in case) alongside the existing CONDITION_NEGATIVE (unless/except/except that), with the correct mirrored blocking rule for each, and remove two further hardcoded keyword regexes found while doing it: the alternative-splitter's literal 'or' match and _clauses' literal 'and' match.
method: lab.common.inference.split_exception/split_exceptions generalized to detect either Operator.CONDITION_NEGATIVE or CONDITION_POSITIVE via find_connectives and return the detected polarity; check_exceptions takes that polarity and applies the mirrored OR-combination rule (negative: any-holds blocks; positive: all-confirmed-false blocks). The alternative-splitter's literal regex match on 'or' and _clauses' literal regex match on 'and' were both replaced with find_connectives-based structural detection. Four cases through lab.common.brain.reason/_clauses directly, re-running the full EXP-083/085/088/089/091 regression suite first to confirm zero behavior change for every existing 'unless'/'except' case.

case1_positive_condition_holds.text: MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes. [rule-provided] Therefore, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes..

case2_positive_condition_blocked.text: policy does not apply: the rule's condition is not satisfied ('If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes.') [rule-provided].

case3_positive_condition_unresolved.text: MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes. [rule-provided] Therefore, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes (the rule's condition is unresolved -- not confirmed either way)..

clauses: the registration and license will be suspended

results_prose: Case 1 ('provided that' phrasing, condition affirmed): decision='supported', text="MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes. [rule-provided] Therefore, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes.." -- clean=True. Case 2 (condition contradicted): decision='supported', text="policy does not apply: the rule's condition is not satisfied ('If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes.') [rule-provided]." -- blocked=True. Case 3 (no context): decision='supported_with_flags', text="MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes. [rule-provided] Therefore, it is lawful, provided that the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes (the rule's condition is unresolved -- not confirmed either way).." -- flagged=True. Case 4 (a non-clausal 'and', 'the registration and license will be suspended'): _clauses returned ['the registration and license will be suspended'] -- correct=True (the old r'\band\b' regex would have returned ['the registration', 'license will be suspended'], two meaningless fragments).
conclusion: EXP-026's real gap -- 'except'/'unless'/'provided that' clauses invisible to the engine -- is closed, but not by treating all three the same, which the stub's own wording would have gotten wrong: 'provided that' is the opposite polarity from 'unless'/'except' (EXP-091), and check_exceptions now applies the correct mirrored combination rule for each. Two further hardcoded keyword regexes (the alternative-splitter's literal 'or' match, and _clauses' literal 'and' match) were found and replaced with the same structural find_connectives detection in the same pass, closing the same class of gap EXP-090/091 closed for 'unless', not just the one instance already flagged.
scale_down: Only CONDITION_POSITIVE's holds-blocks-if-false semantics is wired, matching CONDITION_NEGATIVE's existing scope -- CONCESSION/TEMPORAL_BOUND/CAUSAL remain detection-only, per EXP-090's own follow_ups, untouched here. A third hardcoded word-regex was found (lab/common/intent_signals.py's _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE, `r"[?.;]|\band\b"`, used for splitting an ASK into clauses for the document/identity/total intent signals) but deliberately NOT changed in this exploration -- it is load-bearing for calibrated thresholds across EXP-069/078/079, and fixing it needs its own regression pass against those, not a drive-by edit inside this one.
follow_ups: lab/common/intent_signals.py's _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE has the identical hardcoded `\band\b` pattern -- a real, named instance of the same gap, left open because changing it requires reverifying EXP-069's calibrated MIN_DENSE_SCORE/MIN_SEMANTIC_MARGIN thresholds and EXP-078/079's document-signal scores, not just the split logic itself.
models_used: spaCy en_core_web_sm dependency parser via lab.common.connectives.find_connectives (already built in EXP-090, unchanged here) plus the existing, unmodified MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli NLI call inside check_exception. No new model, no generative model.
